objective: Replace the parallel interruption owner with the repository packet architecture while preserving the accepted pause, confirm, continue, flush, replay, and unclear-input behavior
problem: The current implementation creates interruption-specific event and work channels beside the packet router
Synchronous submit replies create a second ordering and request-response contract inside dispatch
The interruption worker directly calls handler internals and bypasses normal packet routing
design: Delete interruptionOwner, interruptionEvent, interruptionReply, its event channel, work queue, and worker goroutines
Keep one pending interruption candidate as plain requestor-owned state protected by a mutex because control and ingress routes execute independently
Use existing packets for VAD, STT, EOS, user input, turn change, and unclear-input expiry
Add only InterruptionDecisionExpiredPacket as a control packet containing ContextID and Sequence
Have the timer callback synchronously dispatch InterruptionDecisionExpiredPacket through the existing requestor router entry without reading or mutating candidate state
Add internal InterruptionSequence correlation to TurnChangePacket and have handlers mutate candidate state inline before emitting it

Have HandleTurnChange atomically claim the candidate sequence, stop its timer, flush output, rotate context, invalidate old work, clear the candidate, and synchronously route held packets in recorded order
Deliver held VAD boundaries once to the EOS executor after commit instead of routing them through the VAD handler and duplicating STT boundaries
Have HandleFinalizeBehavior stop the timer, advance the sequence fence, discard held evidence, and continue only uncommitted paused output
Do not add helper or utility functions for interruption state transitions
acceptance: No interruption-specific channel, work queue, reply channel, dispatcher goroutine, or direct handler-to-handler dispatch remains
VAD start during assistant output pauses once and opens one 500 millisecond candidate
Meaningful non-filler STT commits through TurnChangePacket
Filler-only or empty STT does not commit
An ended unconfirmed candidate continues output at the deadline
An active candidate commits at the deadline
Late deadline packets cannot affect a later candidate in the same context
Held STT, EOS, and user input packets synchronously traverse the existing router in recorded order with the committed context
Held VAD boundaries reach EOS exactly once and do not duplicate STT start or end packets
A full control queue cannot drop the deadline decision
No public protobuf, streamer interface, or output-control contract changes
non_goals: Changing streamer pause, continue, or flush behavior
Adding public configuration or protobuf fields
Adding helper packages, utility functions, or a replacement interruption component
risks: Control and ingress dispatchers can race unless all candidate fields use the requestor mutex
A timer packet can arrive after cancellation and must be rejected by sequence
Synchronous replay can recurse if candidate state is not cleared before packets return through the router
Cross-lane handler execution can race, so candidate validation and claims must be atomic under the requestor mutex
TurnChange can commit twice unless the sequence and decision state are validated atomically
verification: just agent-finalize with exact changed paths
rollback: Revert amendment 10 and restore the disabled interruption owner implementation. Streamer controls remain compatible and require no rollback.
